summary:
I checked all 51 PLAY.combat.cover tests (50 names, one of them parametrized twice). For each one I re-read the SRD p.15 clause, checked the R-09/R-10/R-11 rulings, and broke the engine in a scratch copy with `scripts.srdloop mutate`. Every test catches at least one targeted break, and I found no wrong oracle: each expected result follows from the SRD text or a register ruling.

I refute 3 tests as duplicates:
- **test_object_covering_the_whole_target_gives_total_cover** has the same setup and the same assertion as test_total_cover_is_not_a_bigger_ac_bonus.
- **test_object_covering_only_half_gives_half_not_three_quarters** adds nothing beyond test_half_cover_ac_is_exactly_two. The engine never works out how much of the target an object covers: the test just sets the label to "half".
- **test_three_quarters_cover_doesnt_help_a_con_save** is the half-cover Con save test with only the degree changed. The Dex-only check runs before the degree is looked at, so one change breaks both. I'm only 0.55 sure here, so a person decides.

Weak spots in tests I kept:
- **Dex save upper bound.** test_half_cover_adds_two_to_dex_save and test_creature_in_the_way_gives_half_cover_to_a_dex_save still pass if Half Cover gives +3 to Dex saves. Only the AC tests pin +2 exactly, because AC and saves share one value in `game.py:233`. Three-Quarters doesn't have this gap: test_three_quarters_dex_save_one_short catches +6.
- **Kept on a narrow margin.**
  - test_creature_cover_applies_through_the_session (`Session.cmd_attack` just calls `C.attack`)
  - test_creature_in_the_way_gives_half_cover_to_a_spell_attack (every break that fails it also fails another test)
  - test_object_covering_three_quarters_gives_plus_five (its only unique catch is the #7 clause number in the log)
- **Earned their place.**
  - test_refused_total_cover_attack_keeps_the_attack_action is the only test that catches the attack being spent before the Total Cover refusal; the session refusal test still passes with that break.
  - test_half_cover_raises_a_pcs_ac_against_a_monster catches cover applied only against PC attackers.
  - test_ally_in_the_way_gives_half_cover_to_the_enemy catches allies of the attacker being ignored.
  - test_small_creature_in_front_of_a_large_one_gives_half_cover catches a size threshold.
  - test_creature_on_a_diagonal_line_gives_half_cover catches line checks that only work on straight lines.

A few verdicts (both 3/4 save tests, test_creature_alone_never_gives_three_quarters' sibling in the 3/4-creature row of the table below, and test_creature_cover_protects_a_pc_from_a_monster's companion tests) rest on breaks I reasoned through rather than ran; each such row says so in its mutation field. The batch and loop runs were denied, so I ran the mutations one command at a time.
